# A test triggers one copy of a node nested loops render by its path, on every
# target a test can execute on: testdata/indexed_trigger_nested.txtar is the
# code. `c.cell[1][0]` is the first copy in the outer loop's second iteration,
# which a flat position among all the copies would put at 1, the "b" in the
# first iteration. The second test renders the loops again first, longer and
# shaped differently, so the checkbox wrappers kept at their positions are
# handed new keys. `#pin`, `#tick` and `#even` are the loop shapes
# testdata/indexed_trigger_nested.txtar describes. `single` writes `#mark` once,
# an id `main` indexes: it keeps its plain invoker, and its checkbox wrapper,
# under no loop, is handed no key.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   3 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   3 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   3 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   3 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   3 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   3 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"
import seq "sngl:seq"

output {
    go {
        bubbletea
        fyne
        gtk4
    }
    kotlin {
        android
    }
    none {
        html
    }
}

const grid = [["p", "q"], ["r"]]

component main node {
    var rows = [["a", "b"], ["c"]]
    var evens = seq.step(0, 4, 2)
    var dots = 2
    var log = ""
    vbox {
        button #swap(text="swap", @click { rows = [["d"], ["e", "f", "g"]] })
        for var row = rows {
            hbox {
                for var it = row {
                    button #cell(text=it, @click { log = it })
                    checkbox #mark(label=it, @change(on) { log = "{it} {on}" })
                }
            }
        }
        for var row = grid {
            hbox {
                for var it = row {
                    button #pin(text=it, @click { log = it })
                }
            }
        }
        for var r = seq.count(2) {
            hbox {
                for var k = seq.count(2) {
                    button #tick(text="{r}{k}", @click { log = "{r}{k}" })
                }
            }
        }
        hbox {
            for var e = evens {
                button #even(text="{e}", @click { log = "{e}" })
            }
            for seq.count(dots) {
                button #dot(text=".", @click { log = "{log}." })
            }
        }
        text(value=log)
    }
}

component single node {
    var show = true
    var log = ""
    vbox {
        if show {
            checkbox #mark(label="x", @change(on) { log = "x {on}" })
        }
    }
}

func testOneCopyOfANestedLoop(t Test, c main) {
    c.cell[1][0].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "c")
    c.cell[0][1].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "b")
    c.mark[1][0].change(true)
    t.assert(c.log == "c true")
    c.pin[1][0].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "r")
    c.tick[1][0].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "10")
    c.even[1].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "2")
    c.dot[1].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "2.")
}

func testAfterTheLoopsRenderAgain(t Test, c main) {
    c.swap.click()
    c.cell[1][2].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "g")
    c.cell[0][0].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "d")
    c.mark[1][1].change(true)
    t.assert(c.log == "f true")
}

func testWhereAnotherComponentLoopsTheId(t Test, c single) {
    if c.mark != null {
        c.mark.change(true)
    }
    t.assert(c.log == "x true")
}

window {
    main
}
